cost: THE SUBJECT LANDS AT 72 AGAINST A TARGET OF 74, error -2 inside the orchestrator's +-3, and the reason is a CHOICE the dispatch asked for: reuse recal_96's load line rather than invent a DEF one. At 17.8 mpg the shared ramp (foot 12, full 24) gives share 0.4833, which prices Kurt Thomas '09 at d_score 63.33 -> DEF 72. To land 74 exactly the share at 17.8 minutes would have to be about 0.62, i.e. a DEF-only foot near 5.4 or a DEF-only full-load line near 21.5 — a second, different load line in the same file, for the same question, two points from the one already ratified. It was not taken. If he wants 74 rather than 72 that is the one-line change, and it moves the same 1,352 cards with him.

THE DEPTH ON THE DEEPEST CARDS IS -20, AND IT IS CONCENTRATED ON ELITE-RIMPROT BENCH BIGS, which is arithmetic rather than taste: the term removes 0.27 x (1 - share) x rimprot, so it bites hardest exactly where rimprot is largest. Dikembe Mutombo '05 (15.2 mpg, rimprot 92, age 38 backup) 82 -> 62 is the extreme, and Arvydas Sabonis '03 (15.5 mpg, rimprot 88) 91 -> 72 the second. Both readings are defensible on the round's own claim — neither man anchored a defence for a quarter of a game — but they are the two places a complaint will come from, and Mutombo '05 at DEF 62 is the single number a later round is most likely to be asked about.

THE HOLE recal_96 LEFT IN ITS OWN TERM IS NOW HALF-CLOSED, and the other half is named. recal_96's COST recorded that recal_91's stretch-big OFF floor 'does carry a raw 0.10 * volume, so a sub-24-minute stretch big keeps a small load credit the rest of the file no longer pays'. On the DEF side the mirror hole is the PERIMETER vector's 0.13 rimprot, which is now deliberately full-price at any minutes — that is the round's central claim, not an oversight: a wing who contests at the rim is being graded on a skill rate, and recal_96 ruled skill rates are not discounted by minutes.

notes: WHAT THE RULING IS ABOUT, in one sentence. Kurt Thomas '09 played 17.8 minutes a night off Al Horford and Zaza Pachulia, scored 4.3 on 5.1 rebounds with 0.7 blocks at BPM -0.3, and had no defensive bar above 79 (perdef 73, rimprot 79, drb 76, discipline 16) — and read DEF 84, 25th of 228 cards in 2009 and above every 32+ minute season of his own career. The number came from one weight: rimprot at 0.40 on the big vector, more than three times the 0.13 the same bar is worth to a perimeter defender.

WHY THAT EXTRA 0.27 IS A LOAD CLAIM AND NOT A SKILL PRICE. d_score's own opening line says why the big vector pays rimprot triple: 'bigs' defensive votes route to rimprot by design, so perdef understates them'. That is a statement about being THE ANCHOR of a defence — the man the other four play in front of — and being the anchor is a BURDEN, measured in minutes, not a rate that is true whether you play nineteen or thirty-nine. So the round splits the weight at the two prices the file already contains: 0.13 is what rim contesting is worth as a skill, paid in full at any minutes to any card, and 0.27 is the anchor premium, paid at recal_96's load share. HIS COUNTER IS ANSWERED RATHER THAN OVERRULED: no skill rate is re-priced by minutes this round. perdef, drb, discipline, perimdisrupt and rimprot's own skill price are byte-identical at every minute count, and a perimeter card cannot move at all.

WHY NOT THE OTHER TWO CANDIDATE FORMS, both measured before this one was applied. (1) THE WHOLE BIG PREMIUM AT LOAD — blending toward the perimeter vector by share, i.e. _perim + share x w x (_big - _perim) — is the obvious mirror and CANNOT REACH THE NUMBER: Kurt Thomas '09's perimeter vector is 67.27 against a big vector of 74.38, so the whole premium is 7.11 of d_score and paying 48% of it lands him on DEF 80, six points above the tolerance band. (2) THE DISPLAY MULTIPLIER AT LOAD (1.1305 scaled by share) reaches only 79, and it would tax every low-minute PERIMETER card in the pool for a finding about bigs. Only the rim-anchor premium is both large enough and narrow enough, and it is the one of the three that has a sentence behind it.

MEASURED ON THE WHOLE POOL BEFORE APPLYING. DEF moves on 1,352 of 10,000 cards, every one of them DOWN (a load discount cannot raise anything; there are ZERO rises), mean -6.29, max -20. By minutes: under 18 mpg 233 of 430 cards moved, mean -6.45; 18-24 mpg 1,119 of 2,367 moved, mean -2.42; 24-30 mpg ZERO moved; 30+ mpg ZERO moved. OFF moves on ZERO cards and no attribute moves — this is a compute_ovr-only round. OVR moves on 1,237, max -10, entirely through the unchanged blend.

THE BOARD'S SHAPE IS UNCHANGED WHERE IT MATTERS. The top 12 by DEF is identical name for name and position for position (six Ben Wallace seasons, Howard '10, two Giannis, Kawhi '16, Davis '18); scout reports ZERO rank flips touching the top 50 by OVR; and the DEF raw top is still a 37.7-mpg card, so DEF_TOP was not re-derived and nothing above the 93 knee moved. The highest-rated card that moves at all is Bobby Jones '84 (23.5 mpg, 83rd on DEF before the round) and he loses ONE point, 95 -> 94; the 296 cards that lose ten or more are ALL under twenty minutes, the deepest at 15.2.

THE CARD THAT PROVES THE SEAM IS SMOOTH. recal_96's COST warned that 24.0 minutes is a corner. On the DEF side the card sitting on it is Dereck Lively II '24 — 23.5 mpg, rimprot 89, share 0.9583 — and he loses exactly ONE printed point, 79 -> 78. Clint Capela '17 at 23.9 loses none. The discount is concentrated where the ruling is: 296 of the 1,352 movers lose 10 or more, and all 296 are under 21 minutes.
